errors.description: Unitarity does not give the stated T-fold SINR improvement. A unitary row has squared norm 1, so matching it preserves white-noise variance and recovers h_n x_{b,n} without an integration gain. The unit-modulus tones in Eq. (7) instead have squared norm T and are not unitary-normalized; these two normalizations are conflated.
errors.evidence: The manuscript states: "If the matrix F_b is unitary" the matched filters "provide the T-fold improvement of SINR." Eq. (7) assigns unit-modulus complex exponentials to waveform samples.

errors.location: Section III.A, comparison following Eq. (3); numerical-results paragraph on temporal combining gains; abstract
errors.description: The comparison counts temporal integration as a replacement for transmit beamforming gain although the longer subcarrier symbols already consume that integration time. Set h_n=1, T=N, unit transmit amplitude, and sample-noise variance sigma^2. Eq. (1) gives beamforming SNR N^2/sigma^2 per symbol; Eq. (4) with orthogonal unit-modulus rows gives N/sigma^2 after matching. Both send N symbols in N samples with total transmit power N. Thus MA-TISK remains a factor N below beamforming in this equal-power, equal-throughput example.
errors.evidence: Following Eq. (3): "For T = N, the same combining gain as with transmit beamforming is achieved." The numerical results compare temporal gains of 12.6 and 12.2 dB to the 12.0 dB beamforming gain. The abstract concludes: "There is no loss in link budget gain compared to spatial beamforming at the transmitter."

errors.location: Subsection C, Transmit Beamforming vs. MA-TISK, opening paragraph
errors.description: The restriction of beamforming spatial multiplexing to the near field is false. In a far-field rich-scattering channel, two angularly resolvable paths can support two simultaneous transmit/receive beam pairs and two spatial streams. Narrow beams can select those paths; they do not necessarily reduce channel rank to one. The rank-one precoder in Eq. (1) describes a single-stream choice and does not establish this restriction on beamforming generally.
errors.evidence: The text asserts: "For transmit beamforming spatial multiplexing is only an option in the near-field." The preceding Spatial Multiplexing subsection instead identifies "near-field communication or rich scattering" as alternatives, and the manuscript explicitly discusses forming multiple beams for distinct propagation paths.

errors.location: Subsection C, Transmit Beamforming vs. MA-TISK; final paragraph on peak data rate
errors.description: The claimed linear growth of peak rate with SNR omits the finite spatial-rank limit of the fixed antenna array. Activating additional streams can trade surplus SNR for rate over a limited range, but once all available spatial modes are used, applying Eq. (9) to each mode gives a finite sum of logarithmic rate terms. The described reuse of existing antennas does not justify unrestricted linear rate growth with SNR.
errors.evidence: Subsection C says "MA-TISK can convert a linear increase in link-budget into a linear increase in data rate" by grouping pairs, quadruples, or 8-tuples of waveforms. The final claim is: "Peak data rate can be made to grow linearly with SNR by means of spatial multiplexing even in far field scenarios." Eq. (9) gives R = log_2(1 + SNR).
